Subject: Escrow sweep / intermediary bank charges & VAT handling (Tacite invoice stream)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking a look on short notice. We're rolling a monthly escrow sweep for our EU/UK vendor payouts and ran into a couple of thorny items related to intermediary bank fees and VAT treatment — figured best to surface them early. Attached are the raw invoice files from this quarter for context.

Key items:
- Current flow: our payer bank sweeps EUR from an EU escrow account into a US intermediary for final USD settlement in some corridors. The intermediary (US) and correspondents sometimes debit a flat SWIFT/intermediary fee before final credit.
- Problem: vendors in the EU/UK expect gross invoice settlement (we bill gross), but beneficiary banks are receiving net amounts (fees debited). That creates a reconciliation gap and VAT reclaim inconsistencies.
- We need to decide: who absorbs the intermediary fee, and how Redwood will present fees on the invoice/credit note so the vendor can reclaim VAT (if applicable).

Questions:
1) Can Redwood route eligible vendors via regional rails (SEPA/UK Faster Payments/ACH) to avoid the US intermediary in EUR/GBP corridors? If not, can you provide a mapping of which rails we should use per country/entity?
2) If an intermediary fee is unavoidable, will Redwood issue a single monthly credit note or gross-up invoice adjustment so the vendor can reconcile VAT?
3) Is Redwood able to issue VAT-differentiated invoices per vendor legal entity (e.g., Tacite Ltd UK branch vs Tacite Sp. z o.o.)?

Suggested outcome: a routing matrix + one of these fee-handling models documented so we can close on accounting.

Attachments: tacite_invoices_Q4.zip (4 files)

Appreciate the help — we have month-end on 31 Dec and need to lock the flow. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Ewa — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We can definitely help; a few clarifying points and an initial set of options below.

Quick clarifiers:
- Which legal entities should Redwood invoice (full registered name + VAT ID) for December? Please provide the preferred invoice entity for each vendor so we can align tax treatment.
- Do you have a target preference on absorbing fees vs passing them through?

High-level options we use operationally (pros/cons inline):
1) Gross-pay model (Redwood absorbs intermediary fees)
   - Redwood pays beneficiary banks the gross amount you invoice; Redwood books the intermediary fees to our cost of goods. We can issue a monthly credit note to reconcile the small variance for your books if needed.
   - Pros: clean vendor experience, VAT treatment aligns with gross invoicing.
   - Cons: Redwood takes variability in bank charges.

2) Net-pay + fee reporting (vendor receives net-of-fees)
   - Redwood pays the beneficiary the net credited amount; we provide a detailed fee report showing intermediary/correspondent fees per payment so Tacite can decide reclaim approach.
   - Pros: predictable cost allocation to buyer/vendor.
   - Cons: vendors often object to reconciling VAT on net receipts.

3) Regional-rail-first routing (recommended where available)
   - Route payments via SEPA/UK faster payments/local rails where possible to avoid US intermediary and SWIFT fees. Where regional rails aren't available, fall back to correspondent routing.
   - Pros: lowers per-transaction fees and VAT friction.

Next steps I propose:
- Ops (cc'd) to draft a routing matrix by vendor/country (attached a starter sheet: proposed_routing_matrix.xlsx).
- Finance (Laura/Vanessa) to confirm VAT handling per entity and confirm whether Redwood should gross-up or pass-through.
- We aim to lock routing + fee model by EOD Tue 2026-12-21 for your month-end.

I'm copying Laura and Vanessa to help with the routing/VAT decisions.

Karthik / Vanessa —

I pulled an initial routing matrix based on Tacite's vendor file and our supported rails. Attached: routing_matrix_v1.xlsx (draft) — quick summary below: 

Summary (draft):
- Poland (Tacite Sp. z o.o.): route SEPA EUR where possible; if beneficiary only supports USD, route via our EU nostro with direct USD conversion to avoid US correspondent where supported.
- UK (Tacite Ltd branch): use Faster Payments / BACS for GBP payouts; avoid GBP<>USD SWIFT unless absolutely required.
- DE/NL vendors: SEPA recommended.
- APAC vendors: many will require USD rails; we will attempt local currency payout via partner rails where supported but expect correspondent fees.

VAT handling notes:
- For EU vendors with valid VAT IDs (intra-community), we recommend issuing gross invoices and routing via regional rails to preserve invoice/gross match — eliminates the need for credit notes in most cases.
- Where net receipts are unavoidable (corridor requires correspondent), finance should determine whether to issue a monthly gross-up credit note or a fee statement (vendor preference). For VAT reclaim, vendors generally prefer a gross invoice + credit note.

Action items:
- @Ben Carter (ops/settlements): please review the matrix and confirm which corridors we can convert to regional rails by 12/21.
- @Vanessa Ortiz (finance): please confirm if Redwood will absorb intermediary fees for Tacite UK entity for December or issue a monthly credit note.
